kartice.povzetek_sl: Plant diseases and pests cause substantial crop losses worldwide, underscoring the need for safe and effective plant protection measures. Plant 5'-3' exoribonucleases (XRNs) could degrade exogenous RNA after uptake, thereby contributing to an intracellular barrier, while viral exoribonuclease-resistant RNAs (xrRNAs) could protect exogenous RNA. However, the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Phylogenetic analysis of eleven plant XRN candidates, together with the A. thaliana XRNs, grouped into two clades designated XRN4-like and XRN2/3-like, and an outgroup comprising two monocot sequences. kartice.naslov: Meiotic recombination rate in Drosophila melanogaster is robust to hypoxic conditions
kartice.povzetek_sl: Meiotic recombination is often described as a plastic trait that responds to environmental stress, but the evidence across stressors is mixed and the role of oxygen availability in particular remains poorly resolved. We tested whether chronic, mild hypoxia alters the rate of meiotic recombination on the X chromosome of Drosophila melanogaster. F1 females were reared from oviposition through eclosion under one of three conditions: an outside-chamber normoxic control (PO2 21 kPa), an in-chamber normoxic control (PO2 21 kPa), and a hypoxic treatment (PO2 8 kPa). To separate genuine meiotic effects from the confounding influence of differential survival, we paired a six-point multiply-marked test cross with marker-free crosses on identical outcrossed backgrounds, directly measured F1 fecundity and F2 egg-to-adult viability, and fit the resulting phenotypic class counts to an extended Cx(Co)m model that accounts for asymmetric meiosis and treatment, marker, and sex-specific mortality. kartice.naslov: Genetic regulation of hepatic retinoid storage is associated with distinct transcriptional networks and liver cellular composition in mice
kartice.povzetek_sl:
Background & AimsVitamin A status is determined by both dietary intake and genetic factors. While genetic variations influencing circulating retinol levels have been reported in humans, the genetic determinants of hepatic vitamin A storage and their biological significance remain poorly understood. We investigated the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying physiological variation in circulating and hepatic vitamin A levels using a genetically diverse inbred mouse population.

Approach & ResultsSerum and hepatic retinol (ROH) as well as hepatic retinyl ester (RE) concentrations were quantified in 20 inbred mouse strains (n=100). Significant strain-dependent variation was observed for all retinoid (vitamin A and its metabolites) measures, with heritability estimates of 0.488 for serum ROH, 0.504 for hepatic ROH, and 0.624 for hepatic RE. Multiomics analyses were performed, including liver transcriptomics, liver untargeted metabolomics, weighted gene and metabolite correlation network analyses, dietary vitamin A supplementation studies on two inbred mouse strains, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing, to identify pathways associated with genetically determined retinoid variations.

kartice.naslov: How Reliable Are Reconstructions of Complex Polyploid Histories? A Benchmark of Phylogenetic Inference Methods
kartice.povzetek_sl: Polyploid phylogenetic inference methods are regularly applied to reconstruct allo- and autopolyploidization events in clades with complex evolutionary histories. To date, however, they have been evaluated mainly on small, simulated networks containing a handful of species and very few polyploidization events. Moreover, the extent to which different methods recover the same evolutionary history from the same data is largely unexplored. Here, we benchmark five existing methods, PADRE, AlloppNET, GRAMPA, MPAllopp and Polyphest, together with GRAMPAIter, an automated extension of GRAMPA developed here that enables its application to histories involving more than a single polyploidization event. We evaluated their agreement on 12 empirical datasets and their accuracy on simulations based on 21 published phylogenetic networks encompassing dozens of species. Simulations varied incomplete lineage sorting, rates of gene duplication and loss, and extent of fractionation. To compare inferred networks, we introduce two measures that separately quantify disagreement in the descendant taxa and parental lineages associated with reticulation events. kartice.naslov: A Method to Correct Internal Standard Normalization Errors in Sequencing Data
kartice.povzetek_sl: Measuring the absolute abundances of microbial communities using only sequencing requires the introduction of an internal DNA standard to all samples. However, any error in the measurement of the internal standard becomes a systematic error propagated to all taxa in a sample. In this work we present a method utilizing random combinations of low-count sequences to detect and correct these systematic errors. When applied to sequencing data from Lee et al. (2025), the method reduced replicate-replicate variance in 66% of samples and did not increase replicate-replicate variance in the remaining samples. This is consistent with a systematic error that is not present in all samples but can be significant when it occurs. Additionally, we show that prior expectations based on the experiment can be incorporated into the method to improve corrections further.

kartice.naslov: UBR5 sustains effector regulatory T cell fitness by restraining the p53 checkpoint
kartice.povzetek_sl: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) restrain antitumor immunity, yet the mechanisms that sustain their effector functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBR5 as a key regulator of effector Treg (eTreg) fitness. Conditional and mosaic genetic models reveal that UBR5 supports Treg proliferation, effector differentiation, and suppressive function. Treg-specific UBR5 deletion inhibits tumor growth and sensitizes tumors to PD-1 blockade. Mechanistically, UBR5 promotes p53 protein turnover through its HECT domain, limiting activation of the p53-p21 checkpoint. Genetic deletion of p53 or p21 rescues key defects in UBR5-deficient Tregs. Single-cell transcriptomic profiling reveals impaired effector-associated transcriptional programs in UBR5-deficient tumor Tregs. Analysis of human tumors further reveals an association of UBR5 expression with eTreg features and nonresponse to immune checkpoint blockade. Together, these findings identify a mechanism linking ubiquitin-dependent protein homeostasis to Treg proliferative fitness and immune suppression, with implications for cancer immunotherapy.
